description_full: Shift4 Payments, Inc. engages in the provision of software and payment processing solutions in the United States and internationally. The company offers a payments platform, which provides omnichannel card acceptance; and processing solutions across multiple payment types, including credit, debit, contactless card, Europay, MasterCard and Visa, QR Pay, and mobile wallets, as well as alternative payment methods, such as Apple Pay, Google Pay, Alipay, and WeChat Pay. It also provides technology solutions, such as SkyTab POS, which provides purpose-built POS workstations; SkyTab Mobile, which provides pay-at-the-table, order-at-the-table, delivery, customer feedback, and email marketing solutions; SkyTab Venue, which provides mobile ordering, countertop POS, self-service kiosk, and digital wallet solutions; Lighthouse, a cloud-based suite of business intelligence tools that includes customer engagement, social media management, online reputation management, scheduling and product pricing, extensive reporting, and analytics; The Giving Block, a cryptocurrency donation marketplace; Shift4Shop, an e-commerce platform that creates a web store and tools to manage product catalog, order fulfillment and inventory management, search engine optimization, and secure hosting; and Marketplace, which enables integrations into third-party applications, as well as loyalty and inventory management. In addition, the company offers merchant operations and support services, including underwriting, onboarding, and activation; training; risk management; and support services. Further, it provides software partner operations and support services, including software integrations and compliance management; partner support; and partner services. The company distributes its products through independent software vendors, internal sales and support networks, enterprises, and value-added resellers. Shift4 Payments, Inc. was founded in 1999 and is headquartered in Center Valley, Pennsylvania.

financial_summary: Shift4 Payments, Inc. is a mid-cap technology business with a $3.4B market cap on $4.2B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +28% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +3.2pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.

Returns on capital run at 7% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, and 22% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $624M in free cash flow — roughly 15 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 5.33× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 4.6× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and thin 1.8× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Management returns a meaningful 10.9% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 32% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and profit capture is only 0.4× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.

mkt: The shares are in a steep downtrend, down 46% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 41% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 65% and a beta of 1.27, it amplifies market moves, though its beta has shifted (1y 0.08 vs 5y 1.50), so read it loosely.

val: The stock trades 79% below its DCF fair value of $211, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 96%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $134 to $334 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.

Earnings yields are mixed: an FCF yield of 18.6% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 4.1% (vs the 8% bar).
The 22 covering analysts target $49.36 on average, 10% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
The price implies 4.6% annual cash-flow growth, 20pp less than the model expects.
prof: ROIC of 7% falls short of the cost of capital of 8.0%, so growth at these returns destroys value; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 4.52).
It runs a 22% gross margin and converts 15% of revenue into free cash flow.
ROE of 8% is amplified by 6.0x balance-sheet leverage (DuPont), so ROIC is the cleaner read on the business.
Operating margin is running 6pp above its own historical average, a peak-margin risk if conditions normalise.
It spends 2.0% of revenue on stock compensation.
hlth: Leverage is heavy at 4.6x net debt to EBITDA ($964.0M of cash against $4.5B of debt), and interest cover is thin at 1.8x.
Warning signs: an Altman Z of 0.96 in the distress zone.
The value-trap profile is elevated (54/100); see the breakdown below.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 28.0% over 3 years and 40.4% over 5 years, so growth is decelerating, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 20%).
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
Capex runs only 0.0x depreciation (0.2% of sales), so the asset base is being harvested rather than grown.
Its Rule of 40 score is 53, clearing the bar for a healthy growth business.
own: Insiders own 32.1%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 96%.
Insiders have only bought over the past year (6 purchases, net $33.6M bought).
